overall_assessment: Track 23 establishes sound methodological foundations for active-learning study prioritisation without compromising screening recall. The empirical calibration curve engine evaluates precision, recall/sensitivity, specificity, FNR, FPR, and Work Saved over Sampling at 95% recall (WSS@95). In simulated benchmark tests, WSS@95 achieved >60% reduction in screening effort while preserving 100% of gold-standard relevant studies. Zero-division guards guarantee mathematical stability across zero-count edge cases. Most importantly, RankingCalibration strictly prohibits automated study exclusion (auto_exclusion_prohibited: true) and mandates human sign-off for prioritisation approval.

findings.description: Calibration curves evaluate static threshold arrays; dynamic quantile-based threshold selection for optimal WSS@95 remains prospective.
findings.recommendation: Incorporate adaptive percentile thresholds when external SYNERGY benchmark data are connected.

findings.description: WSS@95 calculation assumes uniform screening review effort per record; real-world cognitive load varies with abstract length and complexity.
findings.recommendation: Document uniform screening effort assumption as an explicit methodological claim boundary.

findings.description: RankingCalibration contract invariants strictly fail closed if auto_exclusion_prohibited is false or if observed sensitivity fails to meet minimum_sensitivity when approved.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these validation invariants across all execution harnesses and client interfaces.

calibration_notes: Methodologists unanimously endorse the advisory-only prioritisation model, robust WSS@95 calculation, and strict prohibition of automated study exclusion.
